newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ to focus on long term unemployed - Minister.
newsitem.headline: NZ to focus on long term unemployed - Minister.

text.p: New Zealand's priority would be dealing with long-term unemployment, the employment minister said on Tuesday after the release of official statistics showing a rise in unemployment in the March quarter.

"The mix of today's figures and other statistics on long term unemployment ... confirms that duration remains the major challenge for employment policy," Employment Minister Peter McCardle said in a statement.
Unemployment rose to 6.4 percent in March from 5.9 percent in December, acording to Statistics New Zealand's household labour force survey.
Seasonally adjusted employment fell 0.1 percent in the quarter.
Long term unemployed, defined as those out of a job for more than 26 weeks, rose 7.4 percent in the year to March.
McCardle said while economic growth determined the number of unemployed it was clear employment policy could affect the duration of unemployment and this was the prime focus of his portfolio.

"New Zealand can take confidence in the fact that today's 6.4 percent result still puts our official unemployment rate clearly lower than the OECD average of 7.5 percent and seventh out of 21 OECD countries with comparable surveys," McCardle said.

Opposition Labour Party employment spokesman Steve Maharey said the the rise in unemployment and fall in people in jobs spelled trouble for the government's plan to introduce a work for the dole scheme.
"Lack of jobs is the death knell for workfare schemes," Maharey said.
He said current estimates were that the centre-right coalition govenrment's plans would involve between 85,000 and 220,000 people and these would have to revised up as unemployment rises.
